name: AL-03
label: Safe R

key_factors: District leans roughly 23 points Republican, among the reddest House seats
Rogers holds a massive money edge: about $2.6 million on hand versus roughly $9,000 for McInnis
Long-serving incumbent seeking re-election with no visible outside spending against him
Prediction markets price a Democratic win at essentially zero
model.rationale: The district's deep Republican lean, Rogers' incumbency, and his overwhelming fundraising advantage leave McInnis with no realistic path, and markets price a Democratic win near zero even with a favorable national environment for Democrats.
model.watch: Only a major late scandal involving Rogers or an extreme national wave could narrow the margin, though a seat this red is very unlikely to come into play.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.

overview:
Alabama's 3rd District is one of the most Republican-leaning House seats in the country, with a partisan lean of roughly 23 points toward the GOP. Mike Rogers, the incumbent since 2003, is seeking another term and holds an overwhelming financial advantage: about $2.6 million on hand compared with roughly $9,000 for Democratic challenger Lee McInnis, who has raised about $61,000. No general-election polls or expert ratings are available for the race, and prediction markets put Rogers' chances near certain.

The fundamentals leave little room for an upset. Even with a national environment that leans toward Democrats this cycle, the district's deep red tilt combined with Rogers' incumbency and resources points to a comfortable Republican win. The realistic question is the size of the margin, not which party carries the seat.
